source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Focused mainly on administrative and organizational leadership roles across a facility, with a fairly limited direct clinical practice component built into the coursework","B":"A degree whose primary focus tends to be described in fairly vague or inconsistent terms across different nursing school programs and curricula","C":"Original research generation, in much the same structured way a traditional research-focused PhD program is typically designed","D":"Advanced clinical practice and applying evidence to improve clinical outcomes, while the PhD is generally more focused on generating new nursing knowledge through original research"}}
source_row.rationale: The DNP degree is generally more focused on advanced clinical practice and applying evidence-based knowledge to improve clinical outcomes, while the PhD in Nursing is generally more focused on generating new nursing knowledge.
